clue.text: See 17 across
Debauched, unlimited womanising can keep you up at night

definitions.text: can keep you up at night

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted or perverted, so the letters are twisted into a new order
without its limits, the word womanising loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A warning that a life of philandering will cost you your sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips W and G from womanising to leave OMANISIN, and 'Debauched' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness is a condition that stops a person from dropping off, so it keeps them awake through the night.

clue.text: Short match

definitions.meaning: short of weight or lacking something, as in a till being a few pounds under
something used to set a cigarette burning, as in asking a stranger for one

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture that did not last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: under weight or deficient, and the request for a flame to smoke with.

clue.text: Bishop expresses doubt about theologian and his religion

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the doubtful noise wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: um is the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop voices misgivings about a theologian and the faith that scholar follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the hesitation noise wrap round the theologian's letters and HIS; DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a standard crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: The faith founded on the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama is one of the world's major religions.

clue.text: Grumbled as muscle starts to exercise daily

parts.note: beef is slang for brawn or muscle power

indicators.note: the starts of the words exercise and daily are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains while their muscles begin a daily workout routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is informal slang for complaining, so the past tense matches grumbled.

clue.text: They're unclear signs of aging?

parts.note: matters that are not black and white, read as patches of silvering hair that show someone getting older

explanation.walkthrough: Hair turns grey with age, so patches of it are literally signs of aging; the phrase also means situations that are hard to call.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambiguous situations without clear rules are idiomatically described this way, and the question mark points to the hair reading.

clue.text: Snooker — it's my break with cue tip

indicators.note: breaking the words it's my smashes them into a new order
the tip of the cue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A snooker player claims their turn at the table with the end of the cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges ITSMY into STYMI, and 'tip' adds E from cue. Snooker here is a verb: to block or thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To snooker someone is to obstruct them, and to stymie means the same, both coming from ball games.

clue.text: Take away illness? Nice! I'd use acupuncture, perhaps

parts.note: in Britain a Chinese is a takeaway meal from a Chinese restaurant
ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, chronic fatigue syndrome

indicators.note: use is taken as an instruction to put the letters to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient rejoices that needles will draw out their sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' rearranges NICEID into DICINE. 'Take away' looks like a verb for removing illness, but in British usage a takeaway meal from the local Chinese restaurant is called a Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Acupuncture is an example of the traditional healing practices that originated in China; 'perhaps' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Cook departs, out! Good line and curve

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An umpire calls Cook out, a fine stroke and a curving ball both mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the navigator Captain Cook, who did chart this, but it is the anagram signal on D, OUT, G and LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of this kind are meridians, great semicircles running from pole to pole, so each is a curve on the globe.

clue.text: Strain to hear pitiful creature

indicators.note: to hear means the next words are taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: a wretch is an unfortunate, miserable person

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to catch what a miserable creature is saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of the word for a pitiful creature is silent, so it is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain as a verb can mean heave or try to vomit, which is exactly gagging.

clue.text: Catholic reportedly hated getting dressed

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: loathed means detested or hated

explanation.surface: A Catholic, it is said, disliked having to get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing garments is clad, and that is the sense of the past participle here.

clue.text: Physicist's eccentric old relative grasps mass

definitions.note: the possessive here reads as physicist is, naming a scientist

parts.note: fey means whimsical or otherworldly

indicators.note: grasps means holds inside, so the relative's name takes in a letter

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A scientist's odd grandmother holds on to a measure of mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Feynman fits the puzzle's theme: he shared a Nobel Prize for work on the 17/1 theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Feynman was a Nobel-winning American scientist, a theme name for this quantum puzzle.

clue.text: Fruit peeled or pealed?

indicators.note: peeled means stripped of its skin, so the fruit's outer letters come away

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

explanation.surface: A wordplay question about whether a fruit was skinned or a bell sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' removes O and E, the outer letters of ORANGE. The homophone pair peeled and pealed is just play; no sound device is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells that pealed sounded loudly, and the simple past of ring means the same.

clue.text: Funny Gene's headland is uninhabited

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective; the answer is the noun for an uninhabited region

parts.note: Gene Wilder was an American comic actor
a ness is a promontory, as in many Scottish place names

explanation.surface: A comedian's coastal headland has nobody living there.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an adjective standing for the noun for wild, unpopulated land.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild expanse where nobody lives is the classic deserted place, so the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Prunes can wrinkle with time in constant sun

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled word and T go within the faithful word

parts.note: true means loyal or constant

indicators.note: to wrinkle is to crumple, so the letters of can are scrambled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A can of prunes crinkles over time under steady sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrinkle' scrambles can to NCA, and that with T goes 'in' the word for constant. Prunes looks like the dried fruit but is a verb meaning cuts short.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune something is to trim or shorten it, and to cut off the end of a text is the same act.

clue.text: King George enters: I, mad? A foul plot!

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the king's letters sit within the others
foul means corrupt or tangled, so the letters are fouled up

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch storms in, suspecting a wicked conspiracy against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' rearranges the letters of I, mad, A into DIAAM, which the king's letters 'enters'. Plot is the drawing sense, as in plotting a graph, not a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a chart or graph of data, and a drawn chart showing structure is the same thing.

parts.note: the cross-references put the answers to 3, 20 and 23 down in place, giving the sum light plus matter makes a field, and QED is the abbreviation for the theory that describes exactly that

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's smug proof that two numbers add up to a third, signed off with the mathematician's flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the cross-references: 3 is LIGHT, 20 is MATTER, 23 is FIELD. QED looks like 'quod erat demonstrandum', the proof's sign-off, but it is also the standard abbreviation for this physics theory.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicists' theory of how electromagnetic radiation interacts with charged particles is universally abbreviated to those three letters.

clue.text: Qaos regularly going round the bend: 1/2 to 1/10 ratio?

indicators.note: going round means the alternate letters surround the next piece
regularly means taking every other letter of the setter's own name, starting with the first

parts.note: a U-bend is a pipe bend, and U is the shape of a hairpin bend

indicators.note: one half of the following short word, here its first letter

parts.note: the numeral 1 reads as the Roman I, and the slash, as in 'over', turns the letters of ten over into a new order

explanation.surface: The setter's name sends the solver round the bend over a fraction sum, half to a tenth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a sum, and dividing a half by a tenth gives exactly the kind of result the answer names. The final '1/10' is a loose device: I for 1, then TEN jumbled to ENT, the slash read as 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The result of dividing one number by another expresses how many times one goes into the other, which is a ratio.

clue.text: Got back the dodgy midfield? The end of Manchester United

indicators.note: back means the word Got is read in reverse
dodgy means unreliable or shady, so the word the is jumbled

parts.note: the middle letter of the word field

indicators.note: the end of Manchester is its last letter

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbles about a shaky midfield spelling defeat for a famous club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TOG, 'dodgy' turns THE into ETH, the mid letter of field is E, and Manchester ends in R. 'United' looks like the club's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are joined in one body or acting as one are in unison, so united fits.

clue.text: Romantic man in love, into proposal

indicators.note: romantic suggests fanciful and unrealistic, so the letters are given a fanciful order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A smitten man works up to asking for someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' rearranges MANIN, O and INTO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone's name forward for a post or award is a suggestion or proposal of that person.

clue.text: Stuff what's up?

definitions.meaning: a question asking what is wrong, as in what's the trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The word means physical substance, and asking what is wrong with someone uses it as in what is the trouble.

clue.text: In general, people possess nothing — royal speculation?

indicators.note: possess means hold within, so the people word contains the next letters

parts.note: they means people in general, as in they say
O is the figure zero, nothing
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A question about whether ordinary folk owning nothing is a royal guess.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea put forward to explain something, not yet proven, is a hypothesis or conjecture.

clue.text: Old retired painter abandons society

indicators.note: abandons means leaves behind, so a letter drops out
retired means drawn back, so the painter's name runs in reverse

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly artist gives up on social life after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DEGAS into SAGED, and 'abandons' takes away its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people are advanced in years, so the adjective means old.

clue.text: Fellow lied about area of expertise

indicators.note: about means around or mixed up, so the letters of lied are rearranged

explanation.surface: A colleague fibbed over his specialist subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIED into IELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's speciality or discipline is their domain of study, as in an expert in the medical one.

clue.text: Embarrassed men hate making gas

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being put out of order or flustered, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Red-faced men are reluctant to break wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas, CH4, is the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Foolish dictator's colourful past is erased

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: is erased means is wiped out, so a part of the word goes

parts.note: exotic means striking and colourful
ex means former, from the past

explanation.surface: A tyrant's lurid history is wiped from the record, a stupid move.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or senseless behaviour is foolish, and moronic is a close synonym.

clue.text: Monsieur's upset in the finest French town

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, and the M within the French word is flipped

parts.note: creme, as in the French creme de la creme, means the very best
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is distressed in the best French town.
explanation.walkthrough: An M turned upside down looks like a W. CREWE is a railway town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is an English market and railway town, so a town fits.

clue.text: Learn about day of victory in small vessel

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters of Learn are reshuffled

parts.note: VE Day is Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone studies a victory celebration aboard a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LEARN into RENAL. 'vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The blood vessel carrying blood away from each kidney is a modest vein, a small vessel in the body.
